name: Mibsam
overview: Mibsam was a male descendant of Ishmael, identified as the fourth-born son of Ishmael according to Genesis 25:13. He belonged to the tribe named after him, the tribe of Mibsam. There are no additional notes or details about his life or character beyond his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Mibsam means "sweet odor," reflecting a Hebrew meaning that may carry connotations of pleasantness or favor. This is the only recorded name for him in Scripture, and it was not indicated to be given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Mibsam as a son of Ishmael, making him part of the Ishmaelite lineage. Beyond this, no other family relationships or connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mibsam's significance lies primarily in his role as one of the sons of Ishmael, through whom the Ishmaelite tribes were established. His position as the fourth son situates him within the broader narrative of God's covenantal promises extending through Abraham's descendants. Although not a central figure, Mibsam contributes to the genealogical record that traces the fulfillment of God's plan in the Old Testament.
